globalFindings.claim: A model that starts from everyone and adjusts a little for each writer forecast these writers better than population rates. Saved, exposed forecasts; 16,855 decisions from 61 writers. Writer-resampled 95% interval, conditional on saved fits; no new admission.
In planted tests, these instruments found a writer's constant lean, not yet their taste or habits. Synthetic outcomes on fixed human-record covariates; this is not a limit on all possible readers.
In constructed worlds, the largest observed root-cue gain had no leaf evidence and planted cue reliability 0.99. Nominated setting, not confirmation or a real-page reliability estimate.
In constructed worlds, correcting a reader's projection with population rates yielded this largest observed gain. Nominated setting; not a natural-data admission.
In constructed worlds, a shared-shift correction to stated versus revealed preferences yielded this largest observed gain. Nominated setting; not confirmation or a personal-value measurement.
